seo.title: Rascal Phinisi: Komodo & Raja Ampat Yacht Charter
seo.description: Rascal, Rascal Voyages' 30m handmade phinisi from 2015: five cabins for 10 guests, 12 crew, a PADI instructor aboard. Charter from US$12,000 a night.

tagline: A 30-metre handmade phinisi for ten, built in Sulawesi in 2015, with a roof deck made for jumping off
answer: Rascal is a 30-metre traditional handmade phinisi built of ironwood in Sulawesi in 2015, the first yacht of Rascal Voyages. She takes up to 10 guests in five en-suite cabins with a crew of 12, including a PADI dive instructor. She charters whole from US$12,000 a night plus taxes, and Rascal Voyages also sells cabin voyages aboard; Komodo runs May to October and Raja Ampat October to April.
facts: Pak Haji Wahab and Raul Boscarino
5, all en-suite: Master and Cabin 4 on the upper deck, Cabins 1 to 3 on the main deck
Full scuba equipment and an onboard PADI dive instructor; certification on request
Four tandem sea kayaks, four paddleboards, a towable mattress, wakeboard, water skis, snorkelling and fishing gear
Air conditioning and wifi; a library, film library and games
Whole-yacht charter or by the cabin
overview: Rascal is a traditional handmade phinisi, built of ironwood in Sulawesi in 2015 by Pak Haji Wahab and Raul Boscarino. She measures 30 metres overall and Rascal Voyages describes her interior as having "a laid-back luxe vibe reminiscent of the Hamptons".

Five en-suite cabins take up to 10 guests. The Master Cabin, her largest at 5.5 by 4.5 metres, and Cabin 4 sit on the upper deck, each with a king bed and a daybed; Cabins 1 to 3 are on the main deck, two with queen beds and one with a double and a king single bunk. A crew of 12 looks after them, among them a PADI dive instructor.

Life aboard runs across six deck areas: the foredeck by the bridge, a shaded aft deck, the saloon, a sheltered dining deck that seats ten, and a roof deck for yoga, sunset canapés and jumping into the sea. Rascal Voyages sails her in Komodo from May to October and in Raja Ampat from October to April, with crossings to the Spice Islands, the Ring of Fire and Wakatobi between.
why: Rascal Voyages publishes its rates, so a whole-yacht week can be priced before anyone asks: US$12,000 a night plus taxes, with airport transfers, park fees and every activity included and only alcohol extra.

She is one of the few yachts in these waters sold both ways. A couple can take one cabin on a scheduled voyage; a family of up to ten can take the yacht, with a bunk cabin for children and a dive instructor aboard.

days.title: Labuan Bajo to Sebayor Island
days.summary: Board at 11am in Labuan Bajo and sail to Sebayor for snorkelling, paddleboarding or a first dive, watching for white-spotted eagle rays. Sundowners on the roof deck facing Sangeang volcano.

days.title: Sape Bay and the pink beaches
days.summary: The pink beaches by kayak, snorkel or dive, with long-tailed macaques ashore and blacktip reef sharks in the shallows; lunch at a pop-up beach club.

days.title: Komodo Island, Siaba Besar and Gili Lawa Darat
days.summary: A guided walk at Loh Liang to look for Komodo dragons, then drifting with hawksbill and green turtles at Siaba Besar before Gili Lawa Darat.

days.title: Taka Makassar, Tatawa Besar and Seraya
days.summary: Snorkel or dive with manta rays, walk the white sandbar of Taka Makassar, then dinner at a lantern-lit pop-up on a beach by tender.

days.title: Seraya to Labuan Bajo
days.summary: A last morning of sailing and swimming, disembarking after lunch at 1pm, with dolphins sometimes in the wake.

days.title: Sorong to Kali Biru, Waigeo
days.summary: Board in Sorong and cross to Waigeo for the blue river of Kali Biru, Papuan hornbills and sea eagles, and the first sunset on the top deck.

days.title: Mioskon, Kri and Mansuar
days.summary: Snorkel or dive Mioskon or Blue Magic, Cape Kri and Sawandarek in the Dampier Strait, and visit a village with its tribal leader.

days.title: The Yeben archipelago
days.summary: Reefs, turtles and wobbegong sharks, and a private beach club set up for the day.

days.title: Arborek and Penemu
days.summary: Snorkel or dive with manta rays at manta point and Melissa's Garden, then walk up to Penemu's viewpoint.

days.title: Misool: Tomolol and Yilliet
days.summary: A lake of stingless jellyfish in the morning, then the reefs of Yilliet Kecil and Romeo; a night dive or snorkel for the epaulette walking shark.

days.title: Fiabacet and Tomolol
days.summary: Puri Pinnacle for devil rays, the climb to Pucak Harfat over the lagoons, the rock art of Tomolol and a pop-up dinner on a beach.

days.title: Sagof and Balbulol
days.summary: A last dive at Two Tree, then kayaks and paddleboards inside Balbulol's lagoon.

days.title: Sorong
days.summary: Breakfast aboard, then the crew drive you to the airport.

faqs: How much does it cost to charter Rascal?

Rascal Voyages publishes US$12,000 a night plus taxes for the whole yacht, up to 10 guests. Its itineraries say the price includes accommodation, airport transfers, all activities, park fees and excursions; alcohol is extra. James confirms the rate for your dates.
Can we book a single cabin on Rascal?

Yes. Rascal Voyages sells cabin voyages from US$2,500 a night per cabin plus taxes, in Komodo, Raja Ampat, the Spice Islands, the Ring of Fire, the Eastern Lesser Sunda Islands and Wakatobi. Ask James which dates are open.
How many guests does Rascal take?
Up to 10, in five en-suite cabins: the Master and Cabin 4 on the upper deck, each with a king bed and a daybed, and Cabins 1 to 3 on the main deck, two with queen beds and one with a bunk.
When does Rascal sail Komodo and Raja Ampat?
Rascal Voyages' itineraries run Komodo from May to October, from Labuan Bajo, and Raja Ampat from October to April, from Sorong.
